Surah al-Zukhruf (The Adornments) [Meccan, though it is said that verse 45 is Medinan; its verses number 89]. It was revealed after al-Shura.

﴿Ha Mim.﴾ Allah knows best what He intends by it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 2:

﴿By the Book﴾ — the Qur'an — ﴿that makes things clear﴾ — that makes manifest the path of guidance and what is needed of the Sharia (divine law).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 3:

﴿Indeed, We have made it﴾ — We brought the Book into existence — ﴿an Arabic Qur'an﴾ — in the language of the Arabs — ﴿so that you may understand﴾ — O people of Makkah — ﴿its meanings﴾.

﴿And indeed it﴾ is established ﴿in the Mother of the Book﴾, the origin of the books, that is, the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), ﴿with Us﴾. "Ladaynā" (لَدَيْنا) is a substitute (badal) for "ʿindanā" (عِنْدنا), meaning "with Us." ﴿Is indeed exalted﴾ above the books that came before it, ﴿wise﴾, possessing far-reaching wisdom.

﴿Afanaḍrib﴾ [i.e.] numsik ﴿ʿankumu al-dhikr﴾ [the Reminder, i.e.] the Qur'an ﴿ṣafḥan﴾ [meaning] imsākan (withholding), so you are not commanded or forbidden, ﴿an kuntum qawman musrifīn﴾ [i.e.] because you are a people who transgress [meaning] mushrikīn (polytheists) لا
﴿And﴾ there came not ﴿to them﴾ ﴿a prophet﴾ (that is, came to them) ﴿except that they used to mock him﴾, ﴿like the mockery of your people toward you﴾. And this is a consolation for him (ﷺ).

﴿So We destroyed those who were stronger than them﴾ of your people, ﴿in might﴾ meaning strength. ﴿And there has passed﴾ that which came before in the verses, ﴿the example of the former peoples﴾ their description regarding destruction, ﴿so the end of your people is likewise﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 9:

﴿And if﴾ the lam is a lam of oath (lam al-qasam). ﴿You were to ask them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say﴾ the nun of emphasis (nun al-raf') has been omitted from it because of the succession of nuns, and the waw of the pronoun because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. ﴿"They were created by the Mighty, the All-Knowing."﴾ The last part of their answer, meaning: Allah, the Possessor of might and knowledge.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 43 (az-Zukhruf), verse 10:

﴿Who made the earth for you a cradle (mahd)﴾, a bed (firash) like a cradle for the infant, ﴿and made for you therein roads (subul)﴾, paths (turuq), ﴿so that you may be guided﴾ to your destinations (maqasid) in your journeys (asfar).

"And the One who sends down water from the sky in measure"—that is, in the measure of your need for it, and He did not send it down as a deluge—"so We revive thereby a dead land"—We give it life—"thus you will be brought forth"—that is, with the like of this revival—"from your graves alive."

﴿And He who created all the pairs﴾, meaning the kinds, ﴿all of them, and made for you ships﴾, meaning boats, ﴿and cattle﴾, such as camels, ﴿on which you ride﴾. The returning pronoun (*al-ʿāʾid*) has been omitted for brevity. In the first instance it is in the genitive case (*majrūr*), meaning *fīhi* ("in it"), and in the second it is in the accusative case (*manṣūb*).

﴿That you may settle﴾ to settle firmly, ﴿upon its back﴾. He used the masculine pronoun for the back and pluralized "back" (ẓahr) in view of the wording (lafẓ) of "mā" and its meaning (maʿnā), ﴿then remember the favor of your Lord when you have settled upon it, and say, "Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it [ourselves]"﴾, meaning, "capable of it."
﴿And indeed, to our Lord we are surely returning.﴾ (لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ) surely turning back, i.e., returning, (لَمُنْصَرِفُونَ) returning.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 15:

﴿And they have attributed to Him from His servants a part.﴾ Since they said the angels are the daughters of Allah, because a child is a part of its parent, and the angels are from the servants of Allah the Exalted. ﴿Indeed, mankind﴾ the one who says what has preceded ﴿is clearly ungrateful.﴾ Evidently, manifestly disbelieving.

﴿Am﴾ here carries the meaning of the interrogative hamza of denunciation (hamzat al-inkar), and a verb of saying is implied, so the sense is: "Do you say ﴿that He has taken daughters from what He creates﴾ for Himself, ﴿and has chosen (أصفاكم) for you sons﴾?" The word أصفاكم means أخلصكم, "He has purified you for Himself" or "singled you out exclusively." The ﴿with sons﴾ is the necessary implication of your earlier statement, so it is included in what is denounced.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 17:

﴿When one of them is given good tidings of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness﴾ He made for Him a likeness by attributing daughters to Him, because the offspring resembles the parent. The meaning: when one of them is informed of the birth of a daughter to him, ﴿his face becomes dark﴾, i.e. it becomes changed, the change of one who is distressed, ﴿and he is suppressed with grief﴾, i.e. filled with grief. So how do they attribute daughters to Him? Exalted is He above that.

﴿Or﴾: the interrogative hamza of denunciation (hamzat al-inkar) and the waw of conjunction with a clause, i.e., they attribute to God ﴿one who is brought up in adornment﴾, meaning ornament (al-zinah), ﴿and who in dispute is not clear﴾, meaning does not make his proof manifest, owing to his weakness in that respect because of being female.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 19:

﴿And they made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females. Did they witness their creation?﴾ (i.e., were they present?) ﴿Their testimony will be recorded﴾ that they are females, ﴿and they will be questioned﴾ about it in the Hereafter, and punishment will be consequent upon them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 20:

﴿And they say: "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them."﴾ That is, the angels. Our worshipping of them is by His will, so He is pleased with it. ﴿They have no knowledge of that﴾ which they say, concerning the approval of their worship. ﴿They are only guessing﴾, that is, they are lying in it, and so punishment for it is due to them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn, a classical commentary on the Qur'an) on surah 43, verse 21:

﴿Or have We given them a Book before this, so that they hold fast to it?﴾ i.e., the Qur'an, [enjoining] the worship of other than God. ﴿So they hold fast to it.﴾ i.e., that did not happen.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 22:

﴿Nay, they say: "We found our fathers upon a community (ummah)," meaning a religion (millah), ﴿and we are﴾ walking ﴿in their footsteps, guided﴾ by them. ﴿And they were worshipping other than Allah.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 23:

﴿And thus We did not send before you any warner into a town, but its affluent ones said﴾ (the ones made comfortable, i.e., pampered) ﴿like the saying of your people﴾ ﴿"Indeed, we found our fathers upon a community﴾ (a religion, millah) ﴿and indeed we are following in their footsteps"﴾ (following, muttabi'un)

﴿He said, "Even if I brought you better guidance than that which you found your fathers following?"﴾ They said, "Indeed, we reject that with which you have been sent," [meaning] you and those before you. Allah the Exalted said, as a warning to them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 25:

﴿So We took vengeance upon them﴾ i.e., upon those who denied the messengers before you.
﴿And﴾ ﴿when Abraham said to his father and his people, "Indeed, I am free"﴾ i.e., *bari'* (innocent, free of blame)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 27:

﴿Except He who created me, for indeed He will guide me﴾ (إلّا الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي) created me (خَلَقَنِي), ﴿for indeed He will guide me﴾ (فَإنَّهُ سَيَهْدِينِي) will direct me (يُرْشِدنِي) to His religion (لِدِينِهِ).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 28:

﴿And He made it﴾, i.e., the word of tawhid (monotheism) understood from His saying ﴿Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me﴾, ﴿a word remaining among his descendants﴾, namely his offspring, so that there will always be among them someone who affirms the oneness of Allah; ﴿so that perhaps they﴾, i.e., the people of Makkah, ﴿will return﴾ from what they are upon to the religion of Ibrahim, their father.

**Rather, I gave enjoyment to these** (the polytheists) **and their fathers** and did not hasten the punishment upon them **"until the truth came to them"** (the Qur'an) **"and a clear messenger"** (making clear to them the sharʿi rulings (al-aḥkām al-sharʿiyyah, the legal prescriptions of the Sharia), and he is Muhammad ﷺ).
﴿And when the truth came to them﴾ — the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 31:

﴿And they said: "Why not?"﴾ (i.e., "Why was it not") ﴿this Qur'an sent down upon a man of importance﴾ (i.e., of significance) ﴿from the two towns﴾ (i.e., from which of the two towns?) ﴿great﴾ (i.e., al-Walid ibn al-Mughira in Makkah, or ʿUrwa ibn Masʿud al-Thaqafi in al-Ta'if).

Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord? [i.e., prophethood.] It is We who apportion among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and We raise some of them above others in rank, by means of wealth, so that some of them may take others [the poor] in service [sukhriyyan], i.e., made subservient in work for them in return for wages. The ya' in "sukhriyyan" is the ya' of nisba (relative adjective). It has also been read with a kasra on the sin (sikhriyyan). And the mercy of your Lord, i.e., Paradise, is better than what they accumulate in the world.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 33:

﴿And were it not that mankind would become one community﴾ upon disbelief, ﴿We would surely have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful, for their houses﴾ — a substitute for "for those who" — ﴿roofs of silver﴾ — with the sin pronounced with a fatha and the qaf with a sukun, and also with both pronounced with a damma, as a plural — ﴿and staircases of silver﴾ like the steps ﴿upon which they would ascend﴾, meaning they would climb up to the roof.

And for their houses [We would have given] doors of silver, and couches [of silver]—﴿And for their houses, doors of silver and couches﴾. We would have made for them couches of silver, plural of sarir (couch).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 35:

﴿And gold (zukhrufan)﴾ — gold (dhahaban). The meaning is: were it not that disbelief would be a concern for the believers regarding the giving of what has been mentioned to the disbeliever, We would have given him all of that, because the worldly life is of little worth in Our sight and he has no share in the Hereafter, in bliss.

﴿And if﴾ — (wa-in) is a lightened form (mukhaffafah) of the heavy (thaqilah) form. ﴿All of that﴾ — (kullu dhalika) lamma: with the lightened reading (bi-l-takhfif), the ma is superfluous (za'idah); with the heavy reading (bi-l-tashdid), it means "except" (illa), and then in is negating (nafiyah). ﴿Is but the enjoyment of the life of this world﴾ — which one enjoys therein, then it passes away. ﴿And the Hereafter﴾ — the Garden.

"And whoever turns away (ya'shu) from the remembrance of the Most Merciful (dhikr al-Rahman)", i.e., the Qur'an, "We appoint for him a devil (nuqayyid), i.e., We cause to be, for him, a devil, and he is for him a companion (qarin) who never parts from him."

"And indeed they" (i.e., the devils) "surely bar them" (i.e., those who turn away) "from the way" (i.e., the path of guidance), "and they think that they are rightly guided."

In the plural form, there is consideration of the meaning of "man" (مَن).

﴿Until, when he comes to Us﴾, the one who turns away (al-'Ashi) from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, along with his companion on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿he will say﴾ to him: ﴿"Would that"﴾, where "يَا" is for alerting (لِلتَّنْبِيهِ), ﴿"between me and you is the distance of the two easts"﴾, i.e., like the distance between the east and the west, ﴿"how evil a companion you are to me!"﴾

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 43, verse 39:

﴿And it will not benefit you﴾ i.e., you who transgress, your wishing and your regret, ﴿today, since you have wronged﴾ i.e., your wrongdoing by associating partners with Allah in the worldly life has become clear to you, ﴿that you﴾ together with your companions, ﴿in the punishment will be sharing﴾. The "annakum" is a causal clause (ʿilla) with the lām (li-) implied before it, due to the non-benefit; and "idh" (since) is a substitute (badal) for "al-yawm" (today).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 40:

﴿Are you then going to make the deaf hear, or guide the blind, and those who are in manifest error?﴾ Clearly, that is: they do not believe.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 41:

﴿Fa-immā﴾ (then whether): in it there is idghām (assimilation) of the nūn of in (the conditional particle "in") into the superfluous mā. ﴿we take you away﴾ (nadhhabanna bika): by causing you to die before we punish them. ﴿then indeed We will take vengeance upon them﴾ (fa-inna minhum muntaqimūn): in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 42:

﴿Or We show you﴾ in your lifetime ﴿that which We have promised them﴾ of punishment ﴿for indeed We are over them﴾ over their punishment ﴿omnipotent﴾ capable.
﴿So hold firmly to that which has been revealed to you﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿Indeed, you are on a straight path﴾, a way.
﴿And indeed, it is a reminder﴾, an honor, ﴿for you and for your people﴾, because it was revealed in their language. ﴿And you will be questioned﴾ about fulfilling its rights.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 45:

﴿And ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?﴾ That is, other than Him, gods to be worshipped. It has been said: is this to be taken literally, namely that He gathered the messengers for him on the night of the Isra' (the Night Journey)? And it has been said: what is meant is the nations of either of the two People of the Book. On neither of the two opinions was he asked, because what is meant by the command to ask is a confirmation (taqrir) to the polytheists of Quraysh that no messenger from God and no book ever came with the worship of other than God.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 46:

﴿And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs﴾, i.e., the Copts.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 47:

﴿So when he came to them with Our signs﴾ indicating his prophethood

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 48:

﴿And We did not show them any sign﴾ of the punishments, such as the flood, which was water that entered their houses and reached the throats of those sitting, for seven days, and the locusts, ﴿except that it was greater than its sister﴾, its counterpart that preceded it. ﴿And We seized them with punishment so that they might return﴾ from disbelief.

﴿They said﴾ to Moses when they saw the punishment, ﴿O you sorcerer﴾, that is, the complete scholar, because sorcery was among them a great knowledge. ﴿Pray to your Lord for us by what He has covenanted with you﴾ concerning the removal of the punishment from us, if we believe. ﴿Indeed, we are guided﴾, that is, believers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 50:

﴿Then when We removed the punishment from them﴾ through the supplication of Musa (ʿalayhi al-salam), ﴿behold, they broke their word﴾ they violated their covenant and persisted in their disbelief.
And Pharaoh proclaimed among his people, boasting: "O my people, do not the kingdom of Egypt belong to me, and these rivers [of the Nile] flow beneath me? Will you not then see [my greatness]?"

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 52:

﴿Am﴾ (Or) do you not see? And then [do you see] ﴿that I am better than this one﴾, i.e., Musa, ﴿who is contemptible﴾, weak and insignificant, ﴿and who can hardly express himself clearly﴾, [who] does not make his speech clear because of the lisp caused by the live coal that he took in his childhood.

﴿فَلَوْلا﴾ (So why not) meaning "hallā" (why not), ﴿أُلْقِيَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ "be bestowed upon him" (if he were truthful), ﴿أَسْوِرَةٌ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ﴾ "bracelets of gold." *Aswira* is the plural of *siwār* (bracelet), like *aghriba*, which is the plural of *siwār* (as stated). According to their custom, when they make someone their chief (*yusawwiduna*), they dress him in gold bracelets and place a gold collar (*tawq*) around his neck. ﴿أَوْ جَاءَ مَعَهُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ مُقْتَرِنِينَ﴾ "or the angels come with him in succession," meaning following one another, bearing witness to his truthfulness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 54:

﴿So he made light of⁠ his people, and they obeyed him﴾ (istakhaffa): Fir'awn incited⁠ his people [to disbelieve], and they obeyed him in what he wanted of denying Musa.
﴿So when they angered Us﴾ ... they made Us angry.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 56:

﴿So We made them a precursor﴾ (salaf), the plural of sālif, like khādim and khadam, meaning those who went before, as a lesson ('ibrah); ﴿and an example for the later ones﴾ after them, who take their condition as an example, so that they do not venture upon the likes of their deeds.

When ﴿the son of Mary was cited as an example﴾ — this happened when the words of Allah the Exalted were revealed: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾. The polytheists said: "We are content that our gods be with Jesus, since he was worshipped besides Allah." ﴿Then your people﴾, i.e., the polytheists, ﴿from it﴾, from the example, ﴿turn away laughing﴾, i.e., laughing with joy at what they had heard.

They said: "Are our gods better, or is he?" That is, Jesus, so that we would be content for our gods to be with him. "They did not cite it to you except as a dispute." That is, the example (al-mathal), "except as a dispute" (jadalan), meaning contention based on falsehood, because they knew that "what" (ma) is used for non-rational beings, so it would not include Jesus, peace be upon him. "Rather, they are a people given to contention" (khasimun), meaning intensely quarrelsome.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 59:

﴿Inn﴾ (he is no more than) ﴿huwa﴾ ʿIsa, ﴿illa ʿabdun anʿamna ʿalayhi﴾ (only a servant upon whom We bestowed favour) with prophethood, ﴿wa-jaʿalnahu﴾ (and We made him), by his existence without a father, ﴿mathalan li-Bani Isra'il﴾ (a sign/example for the Children of Israel), i.e., like a parable in its strangeness, by which the power of God Most High over whatever He wills is inferred.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 60:

﴿And if We willed, We would have made from among you﴾ [i.e., instead of you] ﴿angels upon the earth, succeeding one another﴾ [by destroying you].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 61:

﴿And indeed he﴾ i.e., Isa (ʿIsa), ﴿is surely a sign (ʿilm) for the Hour﴾ by which it will be known through his descent, ﴿so do not doubt it﴾ i.e., do not be skeptical about it. The nūn of emphasis has been elided for the jussive (jazm), and the wāw of the pronoun (the plural subject marker) has been elided because of the meeting of two sukūns. ﴿And﴾ say to them: ﴿Follow me﴾ (the singular form, in accordance with monotheism), ﴿this﴾ which I command you to do ﴿is a straight path (ṣirāṭ)﴾, i.e., a way (ṭarīq).

And let not Satan avert you (﴿ولا يَصُدَّنكُمْ﴾ — yasrifannakum, i.e., turn you away) from the religion of Allah (﴿الشَّيْطان﴾). Indeed, he is a clear enemy to you (﴿إنّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوّ مُبِين﴾), manifest in enmity.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 63:

﴿When Jesus came with the clear proofs﴾, with the miracles and the laws, ﴿he said: "I have come to you with wisdom"﴾, with prophethood and the laws of the Gospel, ﴿and to make clear to you some of that about which you differ﴾, concerning the rulings of the Torah, both matters of religion and other things. So he made clear to them the matters of religion.
﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is a straight path﴾: *ṭarīq* (way).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 65:

﴿So the factions differed among themselves﴾ concerning ʿĪsā (Jesus): is he God, or the son of God, or the third of three? ﴿So woe﴾ a word of punishment ﴿to those who wronged﴾ disbelieved, by what they said about ʿĪsā ﴿from the punishment of a painful day﴾ painful, causing pain.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 43, verse 66:

﴿Are they waiting﴾ (هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ), i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah, i.e., what are they waiting for ﴿except the Hour, that it come upon them﴾ (إلّا السّاعَة أنْ تَأْتِيهِمْ) — a substitute (بَدَل) for "the Hour" — ﴿suddenly﴾ (بَغْتَة), unexpectedly ﴿while they do not perceive﴾ (وهُمْ لا يَشْعُرُونَ) the time of its coming beforehand.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 43, verse 67:

﴿The intimate friends﴾ in disobedience in the world, ﴿on that Day﴾, the Day of Resurrection, connected to His saying ﴿some of them will be enemies to others, except the God-fearing﴾, those who loved one another for the sake of God over His obedience, for they are friends. And it will be said to them: ﴿O My servants, no fear shall be upon you today, nor shall you grieve﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 69:

﴿Those who believed﴾ is an attributive qualifier (na't) of "My servants" ﴿in Our verses﴾, meaning the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 70:

﴿Enter the Garden, you and your spouses, being made joyful.﴾ "You" (antum) is the subject (mubtada'), and "your spouses" (azwajukum), meaning your wives, ... "being made joyful" (tuhbarun), meaning you will be gladdened and honoured, is the predicate (khabar) of the subject.

﴿They will be served with dishes﴾ meaning bowls (qiṣā‘), ﴿of gold, and cups﴾, the plural of kūb, which is a vessel without a handle, so that the drinker may drink from wherever he wishes. ﴿And therein is whatever the souls desire﴾ with pleasure, ﴿and what delights the eyes﴾ by sight.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 73:

﴿For you therein is abundant fruit, of which you eat﴾ meaning, some of it ﴿you eat﴾, and everything that is eaten is replaced by something in its place.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 75:

﴿Their punishment will not be lightened for them﴾ is lightened (yukhaffaf), ﴿and they will be in it despairing﴾ silent, the silence of despair.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 77:

﴿And they will call out, "O Malik!" (he is the keeper of the Fire), ﴿let your Lord put an end to us,﴾ that is, let Him cause us to die. ﴿He will say,﴾ after a thousand years, ﴿"Indeed you will remain.﴾ that is, abiding in the punishment forever."

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 78:**

﴿Indeed, We have brought you﴾ — i.e., the people of Mecca — ﴿the truth﴾ — through the tongue of the Messenger.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 79:

﴿Am abramū﴾ i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah: have they decided (aḥkamū) a matter (amran) regarding the plot against Muhammad the Prophet? ﴿Then indeed We are decisive (mubrimūn)﴾, i.e., We are firm (muḥkimūn) in Our plot against their destruction.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 80:

﴿Do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private conversation?﴾ That is, what they confide to others and what they say openly among themselves. ﴿Yes indeed!﴾ We hear that. ﴿And Our messengers﴾ — the guardian angels — ﴿are with them﴾, with them, ﴿writing it down﴾ — that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 81:

﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son,﴾ supposing it, ﴿then I would be the first of the worshippers﴾ of the son. But it is established that He, exalted is He, has no son, so His worship (of a son) is negated.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 82:

﴿Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne﴾ [al-ʿArsh], the Kursi (the Footstool) ﴿above what they describe﴾ they say of falsehood, by attributing a child to Him.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 43, verse 83:**

﴿So leave them to plunge in their falsehood﴾ in their vain talk, ﴿and play﴾ in their worldly life, ﴿until they meet their Day which they are promised﴾, in which is the punishment, and it is the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And He it is who﴾ [is] ﴿God in the heaven and God in the earth﴾, with both hamzas pronounced in full (tahqiq) and the first dropped, or the first eased (tashil) to the sound of a "ya." The word إلَه (ilah) means ma'bud (one worshipped). Each of the two locative phrases (fi al-sama' and fi al-ard) is connected to what follows it. ﴿And He is the Wise﴾ in the management of His creation, ﴿the Knowing﴾ of their interests.

Blessed is He (تَبارَكَ): He is exalted (تَعَظَّمَ), **the One** ﴿to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and with whom is the knowledge of the Hour﴾ (of when it will occur), ﴿and to Him you will be returned﴾ (with the ya' and the ta', i.e., read as yurja'un and turja'un).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 43, verse 86:

﴿And those whom they invoke besides Him do not possess intercession,﴾ i.e., those they worship, namely the disbelievers, ﴿besides Allah﴾ i.e., besides Allah, ﴿intercession﴾ for anyone, ﴿except one who testifies to the truth﴾ i.e., says: There is no god but Allah, ﴿and they know﴾ with their hearts what they testified to with their tongues. They are Jesus, Ezra (ʿUzayr) and the angels, for they intercede for the believers.

﴿And if﴾ the lam here is the lam of oath (lam al-qasam). ﴿You were to ask them who created them, they would surely say, "God"﴾. The nun of rafʿ (the nun that marks the indicative mood) and the waw of the pronoun have been dropped from لَيَقُولُنَّ, which originally was لَيَقُولُونَنَّ. ﴿Then how are they turned away?﴾ That is, they are turned away (يُصْرَفُونَ) from the worship of God.

﴿And his saying﴾, i.e., the saying of Muhammad the Prophet. It is in the accusative (naṣb) as a maṣdar (verbal noun) governed by an implied verb, meaning: and he said, ﴿O my Lord, indeed these are a people who do not believe﴾.

**Surah 43, verse 89 — Tafsir al-Jalalayn**

﴿So turn away from them﴾, i.e., disregard them, ﴿and say: "Peace"﴾ — that is, a farewell greeting from you. This was before they were commanded to fight them. ﴿But they will come to know﴾ — with the letter *yā'* (ya‑ta‑lamūna, third person) or *tā'* (you‑plural, second person) — this is a threat to them.
